What a Good SaaS Landing Page Actually Needs

Before you generate anything, it helps to know what you are generating. A SaaS landing page that converts is not a mystery — it is five sections doing five specific jobs, in order.

  • Hero — one sentence that says what the product does and for whom, plus a single primary button.
  • Features — three to five specific capabilities, each with a short explanation of the outcome it produces, not just the mechanism.
  • Pricing section — plans laid out side by side so a visitor can self-select without emailing sales.
  • Social proof — quotes, logos, or numbers that make the claims in the hero believable.
  • Final CTA — a second, low-friction chance to click through, usually right before the footer.

Get those five right and the page does its job. Miss one — usually pricing or social proof — and visitors bounce because they cannot answer whether the product is for them, or whether they can trust it, fast enough.

The One-Prompt Approach

The fastest way to get a page with all five sections is to describe the whole thing in a single prompt rather than building it piece by piece. Name the product, name the audience, and list the sections you want, in order. Kodely reads that as a spec, not a suggestion — it will generate a hero, a feature grid, a pricing section, a social proof block, and a closing CTA in one pass, then you refine from there.

Vague prompts produce vague pages. The more specific you are about the product, the audience, and the exact plans or numbers you want in the pricing section, the less back-and-forth you will need afterward.

A Real Example Prompt

Here is a prompt that produces a complete, usable landing page on the first try:

"Build a landing page for a SaaS called FlowTrack, a project management tool for remote teams. Hero headline about eliminating status-update meetings, with a signup button. A three-column feature section covering Kanban boards, async daily updates, and time zone-aware scheduling. A three-tier pricing section: Free, Team at $12 per user per month, and Business at $24 per user per month. A social proof section with three short customer quotes. A final CTA section repeating the signup button."

That is roughly 70 words, and it maps directly onto the five sections above. Kodely turns it into a working page in one build.

What Kodely Actually Generates

Every project starts from a real foundation codebase — hand-built UI primitives such as Button, Card, Section, and Nav — and Kodely writes on top of it in Vite, React 19, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS v4. The output is real component files: actual .tsx source, not a design rendering. You can open the code view in-app and read or copy every file it wrote.

As the AI builds, the live preview shows the actual compiled app, not a placeholder screenshot. Credits are metered from real AI cost, and a build that fails to compile is never charged — Kodely attempts one automatic repair first. A typical first build for a landing page like this runs roughly 100 to 150 credits.

Customizing via Chat

Once the first version is up, keep going in plain English: shorten the hero headline, reorder the pricing tiers so Team sits in the middle and gets highlighted, add a fourth feature card for integrations. Each change edits the real components behind the scenes — there is no separate visual editor, everything goes through chat, and each result appears in the live preview immediately.

Every successful generation is saved as a checkpoint. If a change makes the page worse, roll back to the previous version for free — no credits spent, no lost work.

Publishing It Live

When the page looks right, click Publish. Kodely scans the build for accidentally leaked secrets or API keys, then puts it live at a real public URL on a <name>.kodely.site subdomain — included, free, with no separate hosting step. There is currently no custom domain support, so the site lives at that subdomain rather than your own domain.

Important: This Builds the Marketing Site, Not the SaaS App

Be clear about what you are asking for. A prompt like the one above produces a real, working landing page — the marketing site that explains your SaaS and captures interest. It does not produce the SaaS product itself. Kodely does not generate backends, databases, user authentication, or payment processing, so an actual signup flow, a working free trial, or billing logic are outside what it builds today. Use Kodely for the page that sells the idea and collects interest, and wire up the real product separately.

Do I need to know how to code?

No. You describe the page in plain English and Kodely writes the React and TypeScript code for you. You can view the source in-app if you want to read it, but you never have to.

Can I use my own domain?

Not yet. Published sites live on a free <name>.kodely.site subdomain.

Can I download the code?

Not currently. You can view and copy individual source files from the in-app code view, but there is no zip export or full-project download yet.

Will this page actually let people sign up for my SaaS?

It will collect interest with whatever call-to-action and copy you design, but Kodely does not generate the backend, database, authentication, or payment processing needed for a real signup or trial flow. Treat it as the marketing front door, not the product.

What does it cost?

New accounts get 750 free credits with no credit card required — enough for a first landing page build and several rounds of edits, since a build typically runs 100 to 150 credits. Beyond that, top-ups start at $9 for 500 credits, and credits never expire. See pricing for the full breakdown.

What if the build fails?

You are not charged. Kodely automatically attempts one repair, and failed compiles never consume credits.

Build your SaaS landing page free and see the real code and live preview in minutes.
